analysis.title: "We're Not In Kansas Anymore": Staples Soar Most Since The Dot-Com Peak... And BTIG Says The Flush Hasn't Even Started
key_insights: BTIG's Jonathan Krinsky calls the market 'Violent Rotation, but Not a Durable Bottom'. Consumer staples had their best month since October 2000 (+11% in October), the Nasdaq 100 printed its first negative outside month at an all-time high since 2021, semis are down four weeks in a row, and the VIX has not closed above 20.

On Friday the NDX closed down roughly 3.5% and the S&P lost 138 points to 7,582 but held above its September lows. Krinsky sees risk to the 200-DMA near 7,300 (also the June-July lows), about 3.6% below Friday's close, and expects correlations to rise on the downside.
QQQ closed at $690, about $11 above its 200-DMA. Krinsky expects it to test the 200-DMA and more likely undercut it toward its July lows.

SOXX fell from about $517 on Wednesday morning to $471.51 at Friday's close and is below its 200-DMA. A break of the six-month range would target the April breakout point at $365-400, which is 15% to 23% lower. The equal-weight semis ETF XSD is on its second trip below its 200-DMA this year and nears a third test of its July lows.
Morgan Stanley's AI Beneficiaries basket (MSXXAIB) is breaking down from a multi-month top at 557 versus a 200-DMA near 598. The SPHB/SPLV ratio has broken its uptrend held since spring.

The Nasdaq 100 made a new all-time high in October and closed the month below September's low. In seven prior cases since 1985, the NDX was higher six months later (average +14.6%, median +11.7%), but each had a drawdown of at least 8.5% (average max drawdown 14.9%, median 13.1%, worst 27.2% in 1990).

No capitulation signals have fired. The Nasdaq Daily Sentiment Index closed at 44, the lowest since July (it was 30 in July and 12 in March). There has been no 80%+ NYSE downside-volume day in nearly a year, and Krinsky wants at least one before playing offense.

Credit is weakening beyond the lowest quality. Investment grade tech spreads are nearing their 2022 wides, and average high yield spreads are at 340bps, the widest of the year and since spring 2025. Goldman's credit team reached a similar conclusion on Friday.

Defensives look stretched. Staples rose more than 11% in October. BofA's derivatives team warned on Thursday that staples and healthcare are in bubble-risk territory last seen at the dot-com peak. XLV is 16.5% above its 200-DMA, essentially tying the widest spread in its history, and is exposed whether the market flushes or AI rebounds.

Utilities are into key resistance after an 11% rally, and Krinsky says the risk/reward has totally shifted. Gold broke below its summer lows, completing a topping pattern, with a target near $3,500/oz versus Friday's $3,899. Silver at $49 has downside risk toward $40.

Polymarket odds of a Democrat winning the Kansas Senate race rose to 54% from about 20% in late August. A blue sweep would be a headwind for the data center build-out. Krinsky says the further semis and AI fall into Tuesday's election, the more likely he covers tactical shorts in the AI complex, though he still sees meaningful downside in semis and expects counter-trend rallies after four down weeks.

sector_views.rationale: SOXX is below its 200-DMA and a break of the six-month range targets $365-400. Counter-trend rallies are likely after four down weeks, but BTIG sees meaningful downside.
Staples gained more than 11% in October, the best month since October 2000, and BofA flags bubble risk in defensives.
XLV is 16.5% above its 200-DMA, nearly the widest in its history, and is a likely culprit for an unwind in a correlation-one selloff or an AI rebound.
After an 11% rally the sector is into key resistance and the risk/reward has shifted.

Silver is weaker than gold, per Krinsky.

tension_points.bull_case: With SOXX down four weeks in a row, counter-trend rallies will likely occur, and the more semis fall into the election the more of a Democratic sweep is priced in.
tension_points.bear_case: No sentiment washout, no 80% downside-volume day in a year, junk spreads at the year's wides and defensives at dot-com extremes mean no durable bottom has formed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break of the SOXX six-month range to the downside, and a correlation-one selloff that takes the S&P toward its 200-DMA near 7,300.

tension_points.bull_case: All seven prior negative outside months at an all-time high were positive six months later, averaging +14.6%.
tension_points.bear_case: All seven also saw at least an 8.5% drawdown over the next six months, and two saw 20% or more.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An 80%+ NYSE downside-volume day or several would signal capitulation and mark a washout.
